source: reviews/claude/tools/m3/endgame_teach/ (build_raw.mjs, assemble.mjs; ideas, hand-chosen tries and notes in authored_ideas.mjs and authored_notes.mjs)
author: Claude, M3 builder A2, 2026-11-12
results: every legal move at every solver step, from the solver's view: win, draw or loss (no cursed wins or blessed losses occur)
tries: up to four per step: moves that change the result, most natural first (hand-chosen, named in the drill explanation for that step, near misses next to the answer square, checks, captures, pawn moves, king moves towards the action), plus in mate drills checks that only delay the mate
lines: up to 10 plies after the try: the winning side mates fastest and the losing side resists longest (DTM); in a drawn position the side trying to win pushes a pawn safely in a pawn ending, otherwise plays the drawing move that leaves the fewest holding replies, and the defender prefers captures, pawn moves, checks, then king moves towards the square in front of the pawn; a drawn line stops once no pawns are left and material is level
notes: written by the builder from each line; assemble.mjs and tests/m3_endgame_teach.test.ts check every move and claim a note makes
